title: Mount a gripper module on a manual tool changer and lock it
instruction: Mount the spare gripper module on the tool changer. Pick the blue module up from its tray by its two black jaws, set its tongue down on the entry ledge at the front of the slot on the master plate, and slide it back along the slot until it stops against the end stop. Hold it there: a spring plunger in the end stop pushes it back out as soon as it is let go. With your other hand, swing the red locking lever by its black knob a quarter turn round to the right, until the lever rests against the black stop pin; its steel tooth then goes into the notch in the module's right side and holds the module home. Then let go with both hands.
context: Swapping end effectors on a quick-change plate is a routine chore in any robot lab, and the lock is easy to miss: an unlocked tool falls off the first time the arm moves. Robots that can re-tool robots shorten the loop of building and running them.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Tool changer, fixed: a grey steel stand 11 x 7 cm and 3 cm tall (x 0.220 to 0.330, y 0.005 to 0.075). On it, an aluminium T-slot guide 6 cm wide (y 0.010 to 0.070) along x on the line y = 0.04: two side walls 6 mm tall from x 0.220 to 0.320 with a 23 mm slot between them, and, from x 0.270 to 0.320, two lips 4 mm thick on the walls leaving a 13 mm opening; the lips' top is 4 cm above the table. The 5 cm in front of the lips is the entry ledge. End stop: an aluminium block 10 mm thick, 6 cm wide, 6 cm above the table, its face at x 0.320. Spring plunger: a steel head 10 mm square, centred 4.8 cm above the table on the slot's centre line, sticking out 12 mm from the end stop's face; pushed flush it presses with 1.2 N (100 N/m). Locking lever: 1 cm thick, underside 4.2 cm above the table, on a vertical pivot pin at (0.255, 0.011). At the start its red handle, 8 mm wide, runs 88 mm from the pin towards the robots and carries a black knob 10 mm across and 25 mm tall at (0.170, 0.011), top 7.7 cm above the table; its steel hook arm, 6 mm wide, runs 50 mm from the pin to the right, ending in a tooth 9 mm long pointing away from the robots. The lever turns only anticlockwise seen from above, up to a stop at 90 degrees (locked: handle pointing right, knob at (0.255, -0.074), hook arm along the slot's right side, tooth pointing left). A black stop pin 8 mm across at (0.2635, -0.047) on a steel bracket off the stand marks the locked handle's place. Lever hinge friction 0.02 N m: it stays where it is left. Tray, fixed: grey aluminium, 8 x 8 cm, 4 mm thick, centred at (0.20, 0.20). Gripper module, loose, 100 g, standing on the tray centred on it, its length along x: an aluminium T-tongue (a plate 40 x 20 x 5 mm under a neck 40 x 10 x 6 mm), on it a blue anodised aluminium body 40 x 40 x 30 mm, and on top two black jaw fingers 14 mm long (x), 8 mm wide and 20 mm tall, 10 mm apart (26 mm across outside); 6.1 cm tall in all. A notch in the body's right side, 9.5 mm long, 4 mm deep and 14 mm tall up from its underside, starts 17.5 mm behind its front face. No other objects.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest. The module is on the guide if its tongue is in the slot: tilted no more than 5 degrees, its underside within 2 mm of the slot's floor, its centre line within 2.5 mm of the slot's, and at least 10 mm of the tongue under the lips. 0 if it is not on the guide. 0.25 if it is on the guide but its back face is more than 3 mm from the end stop's face. 0.5 if it is within 3 mm and the lever is not locked. 1.0 if it is within 3 mm and the lever is within 2 degrees of locked (its handle against the stop pin). Locked with the module home, the plunger leaves it about 2 mm off the stop, held by the tooth; unlocked, it pushes it out about 8 to 10 mm.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Swing the lever back until its handle points at the robots, slide the module out of the slot and stand it upright on its tongue, centred on the tray, jaws up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. A squared-off T-slot stands in for a dovetail, with 1 to 1.5 mm clearances and no chamfers. The lever's lock is the tooth in the notch; a real changer's cam also draws the tool tight, which is not modelled. The plunger is a sprung slide. The module is one rigid body of uniform density with fixed jaws and no cable or air connections.
